title: What tasks can a legal assistant handle?
excerpt: From a busy inbox to documents waiting for review, here’s where a legal assistant can help and how to make the handover work.
seoTitle: What tasks can a legal assistant handle?
seoDescription: See which tasks a legal assistant can take off your desk, from inbox management to document preparation, with clear supervision and a simple handover.

sections.heading: Start with the work that keeps piling up
paragraphs: What tasks can a legal assistant handle? Think about the jobs still on your list at the end of a busy day. The inbox you haven’t sorted. The documents that need tidying up. The client who is waiting for a meeting time. These are often the first places where an extra pair of hands can make a difference.

A legal assistant can help with the everyday work around your matters, so you have more time to focus on your clients. The best starting point is a short list of recurring tasks, with a clear idea of what a finished job looks like. Here are a few ways that can work in practice.

sections.heading: Keep your inbox and calendar in order
paragraphs: An assistant can sort incoming messages, flag items for your attention, organise meeting requests and keep your task list up to date. Instead of opening your inbox and working out where to begin, you can start with a short summary of what needs you.

For example, you might ask them to separate scheduling requests from matter correspondence and collect questions for your review. Show them what your firm treats as urgent and who to contact when you are unavailable. Agree how dates are checked before they go into the calendar, especially when a matter involves a deadline.

sections.heading: Get files and documents ready for review
paragraphs: Keeping files organised takes time, even when the work is straightforward. An assistant can maintain folder structures, update records, check that the right documents are saved and help everyone find the current version.

They can also help prepare drafts, proofread documents and gather research for your review. Give them the relevant materials, an example of the format you want and a clear place to leave questions. For a document handover, that might mean a clean draft, a list of missing information and a note about anything that needs your decision. You still review and approve the work before it is used.

sections.heading: Make client follow-ups easier to manage
paragraphs: Client intake and follow-ups are easy to put off when your day fills up. An assistant can help collect information, organise appointment times and prepare routine administrative messages using the process your firm has agreed.

Be specific about which messages they can send and which need approval. A request for a convenient meeting time is different from a question about a client’s legal position. Make it easy for the assistant to pass those questions to the right lawyer, rather than leaving them to work out an answer. Billing support can follow a similar routine, with information gathered and records prepared for the person who checks the invoice.

sections.heading: Be clear about what stays with you
paragraphs: At Keel, our team members are law graduates who work under your direction and supervision. They do not provide legal advice or practise as licensed lawyers in your jurisdiction.

That means the handover needs to cover more than the task itself. Say who reviews the work, what the assistant can do independently and when they should pause and ask. The scope should suit the person’s skills, your firm’s procedures and the requirements that apply to your practice. Clear boundaries give both of you a better working day.

sections.heading: Start small, then build a routine
paragraphs: Choose two or three tasks to hand over first. Walk through a real example, explain where the information lives and review the first few pieces of work together. When you spot something that could be clearer, update the instructions while it is fresh.

A short daily update can keep things moving: what is done, what needs your review and what is waiting on someone else. Once that routine is working, you can add more tasks without trying to change everything at once.

If you are thinking about legal support for your firm, bring us a few examples of the work taking up your time. We’ll talk through your workload, tools and hours, and help you work out where to start.
